title: (Sequential) Joint Detection and Estimation: Classic Results and New Directions
summary: We provide an overview of the problem of jointly testing two hypotheses and estimating a parameter of the selected model. Such problems arise in a variety of applications. First, we present a conceptual introduction to suboptimal and optimal procedures for joint detection and estimation. A numerical example illustrates the advantages of the optimal procedure over suboptimal ones. Next, we discuss how more advanced problem formulations affect the presented results.
